title: DCP Multi-Copy Schur-Weyl Symmetric-Subspace Projection and Classical r-Sample Majority Bridge
claims: The r-copy symmetric subspace projection probability P(Sym^r | theta, gamma) = sum_{k=0}^r ((1+gamma)/2)^{r-k} ((1-gamma)/2)^k is strictly independent of the secret phase theta.

For commuting half-period targets (theta in {0, pi}), classical r-sample Binomial majority voting on single-copy X outcomes achieves the exact 2^r x 2^r collective quantum Helstrom trace distance, whereas non-commuting quadrature targets (theta = pi/2) on matched headers exhibit a scoped collective Schur-Weyl gain subject to r-way header collision costs.
